proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R)$, an abelian category by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $P=\prod_{n\geq1}F_n$ with projections $q_n$. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], this product exists, has sections $P(U)=\prod_nF_n(U)$, and countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Define $d:P\to P$ on sections by $d_U((x_n)_n)=(x_n-t_{n,U}(x_{n+1}))_n$. Since the $t_n$ are module-sheaf morphisms, these formulas are linear and commute with restriction; thus they define the asserted $1-s$. Write $L=\varprojlim_nF_n$ and $i:L\to P$ for the tuple of its projections. By [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], $L(U)$ is exactly the module of compatible sequences.

proof.text: Choose an affine weakly contractible covering family using [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family]. An epi of module sheaves becomes a locally surjective map of underlying set sheaves by Mathlib Sites.EpiMono and module-sheaf sheafification. The private large_section_surjective lemma transports weak contractibility to larger coefficient universes: sheafify a small coproduct of representables indexed by arrows of the image sieve, lift the identity section using weak contractibility, and map that lift into the original larger sheaf using compatibility of sheafification with universe lifting. Thus each transition is surjective on each covering object. No preservation-of-colimits theorem is required.

proof.text: On a fixed $W_a$ choose, for each $n$, a set-theoretic section $\sigma_n$ of the surjection $t_{n,W_a}$ in step 2. Starting with $x_1=0$, define recursively $x_{n+1}=\sigma_n(x_n-y_n|_{W_a})$. Then $t_{n,W_a}(x_{n+1})=x_n-y_n|_{W_a}$ for every $n$, so $d_{W_a}((x_n)_n)=y|_{W_a}$. The tuple is a section of $P(W_a)$ by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. The chosen sections need not be linear or natural: they are used only to produce a local preimage of this section $y$. This is ordinary countable recursion and choice.

source.place: Tag 0947 (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), coordinatewise lifting on weakly contractible objects; explicit recursion for 1-s

proof.text: The coordinate recursion gives local surjectivity on underlying set sheaves over a covering family, hence a sheaf epimorphism, reflected by the faithful forgetful functor from module sheaves. Independently, for any fork annihilated by 1-s, its product coordinates satisfy the adjacent transition equations. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles them into a cone, and the inverse-limit universal property produces the unique kernel lift. The limit-to-product map is therefore mono and is the kernel of 1-s; together with the epi this proves the displayed short complex short exact.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] to obtain CountableAB4Star for module sheaves. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] says Q maps the canonical termwise product cone to a limit cone. The single-complex functor preserves limits by Mathlib HomologicalComplexLimits. Transport this preservation through DerivedCategory.singleFunctorIsoCompQ and Discrete.compNatIsoDiscrete to obtain exactly the fan with degree-zero localized projections. source.place: Tag 07KC (lemma-products), termwise products in the derived category

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] to the short exact sequence of step 4 in $\mathcal A$. It yields a distinguished triangle $L[0]\xrightarrow iP[0]\xrightarrow dP[0]\xrightarrow\delta L[0][1]$. On composing $d$ with the $n$-th product projection of step 5, its sectionwise formula gives $q_n\circ d=q_n-t_n\circ q_{n+1}$. Thus its middle arrow is precisely the transition endomorphism $1-s$ in [def-weil-derived-limit], with the sign and indexing used there. The triangle is consequently a Roos triangle in that definition. This proves clause 2, with the specific derived limit $(L[0],i,\delta)$; no categorical inverse-limit universal property for arbitrary objects of $D(\mathcal A)$ is being asserted.

For the compatible sheaf maps $g_n:G\to F_n$, the inverse-limit universal property in [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] supplies a unique sheaf map $h:G\to L$ with $p_nh=g_n$. Its composite with $i$ has all coordinates $g_n$, so after placing sheaves in degree zero it equals $(g_n)_n$ by the product universal property [def-weil-category-product] and step 5. Conversely, every derived morphism $u:G[0]\to L[0]$ comes from a unique sheaf morphism $u_0:G\to L$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. If $iu=(g_n)_n$, composing with each projection gives $S(p_nu_0)=S(g_n)$, where $S$ is the degree-zero embedding. Its faithfulness gives $p_nu_0=g_n$, hence $u_0=h$ and $u=S(h)$. This proves exactly the uniqueness of clause 3 for the derived limit chosen in clause 2. The parenthetical vanishing also has the stated sign: for the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], $G[0]$ is in $D^{\leq0}$ and $P[0]$ in $D^{\geq0}$; axiom 2 of [def-weil-t-structure] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(G[0],P[0][-1])=0$. Here $P[0][-1]$ is supported in cohomological degree $1$, not degree $-1$. Finally, if $u$ and $v$ both have the prescribed composite with $i$, the uniqueness just proved gives $u-v=0$. Writing $b:P[0][-1]\to L[0]$ for the shifted connecting arrow of step 6 (with the rotation sign), this difference is explicitly $b\circ 0$, where $0:G[0]\to P[0][-1]$. This verifies the parenthetical factorization without invoking any unstated exactness theorem for representable Hom.
